acceptance-criteria.criterion: When a link is posted with a url and a title, the system shall store it and return 201 with an integer id, the submitted url and title, and a created_at timestamp.
When a link is posted with a url and no title, the system shall store it with a null title and return 201.
If a link is posted with no url field, then the system shall return 422 and store nothing.
If a link is posted with a url that does not parse as an absolute http or https URL, then the system shall return 422 and store nothing.

context.data-model: Link(id integer pk, url text not null, title text null, created_at timestamp not null)
context.prd-excerpt:
Feature: Save a link (slug save-link).
User story: As someone collecting links, I want to store a URL with an optional title, so that I can come back to it without keeping a browser tab open.
Description: A POST endpoint that accepts a URL and an optional title, stores it, and returns the stored record including its generated id and creation timestamp.
The URL is the only required field. If no title is supplied the field is stored as null rather than being derived from the page, because fetching the page would make the endpoint depend on the network.
Considerations (from the feature's notes, NOT an acceptance criterion): duplicate URLs are allowed. Deduplication sounds obviously desirable but needs a rule for what to do with the existing record's tags and timestamp, and that decision is out of scope. This endpoint must therefore accept the same url twice and create two rows - do not add a uniqueness check.
Path basis, from the analysis pass: "The description states a POST endpoint accepting a URL and optional title. Method and behaviour are stated; the path string is inferred from the Link entity name. No /api prefix - the PRD never mentions one."

task.objective: Add the POST /links route handler to app/api/links.py. It accepts a url and an optional title, stores one Link row, and returns 201 with the generated integer id, the submitted url, the title (null when none was supplied) and a created_at timestamp. A payload with no url, or with a url that is not an absolute http or https URL, is rejected with 422 by the LinkCreate schema before the handler runs, so nothing is stored.

requirements.requirement: Modify `app/api/links.py`. Keep the existing `router = APIRouter(tags=["links"])` line exactly as it is - do not add a prefix and do not re-create the router.

Add these imports to `app/api/links.py`:
from datetime import datetime, timezone from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, status from sqlalchemy.orm import Session from app.db import get_db from app.models.link import Link from app.schemas.link import LinkCreate, LinkRead

Add the handler:
@router.post("/links", response_model=LinkRead, status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED) def create_link(payload: LinkCreate, db: Session = Depends(get_db)) -> Link: ...
The path is exactly `/links`. There is NO /api prefix - the PRD never mentions one. The router created by L3-002 carries no prefix either, so the handler declares the full path itself.
The success status is 201, declared via `status_code` on the decorator so that FastAPI documents it and returns it without the handler constructing a Response. The response_model is `LinkRead`.

The handler body must, in this order: 1. Build `link = Link(url=payload.url, title=payload.title, created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(tzinfo=None))` 2. `db.add(link)` 3. `db.commit()` 4. `db.refresh(link)` - this is what populates the autoincremented `id` 5. `return link` - return the ORM instance; LinkRead's from_attributes handles it
Do not build a dict by hand, and do not set `id` yourself.
The tzinfo is stripped from created_at deliberately. A SQLAlchemy `DateTime` column on SQLite is timezone-naive, and handing it an aware datetime round-trips an offset suffix that the SQLite date processor then fails to parse on read. Storing naive UTC also keeps the value comparable for L3-004's "most recently created first" ordering without mixing aware and naive values.

Pass `payload.title` through unchanged. When the client omitted the title, `payload.title` is already `None` and must be stored as SQL NULL and reported as JSON `null` - do not substitute an empty string, and do not derive a title from the url or by fetching the page.

Write NO validation code in the handler. Do not check that url is present, non-empty or well-formed - LinkCreate already does all of it, and duplicating the check in the handler would produce a 400 or 500 for a case the criteria require to be a 422.

DUPLICATE URLS ARE ALLOWED. Do not query for an existing row with the same url, and do not return 409. Posting the same url twice must create two rows with two different ids. This comes from save-link's notes/considerations block - deduplication needs a rule for what to do with the existing record's tags and timestamp, and that decision is out of scope. It is an implementation constraint, not an acceptance criterion.

Add ONLY the POST handler to app/api/links.py. GET /links is L3-004 and POST /links/{link_id}/tags is L3-006; both reopen this same file afterwards. Do not anticipate them. Do not modify app/main.py - the router object is already included there, so a route registered on it is served automatically.

test-requirements.test:
Test-first. Write every test below into `tests/test_save_link.py` BEFORE adding the handler to app/api/links.py, run `pytest tests/test_save_link.py` and watch all five fail, then add the handler until they pass. Runner: pytest.
Note the ordering conflict recorded at the top of the dependencies section: in the declared layer order these tests fail on a missing `tests/conftest.py` and a missing `app/models/link.py` rather than on the missing handler, and they cannot go green until layer 4 is merged. Write them against the contracts as given regardless; do not weaken an assertion to make it pass without layer 4.
Imports for the file:
from datetime import datetime from sqlalchemy import func, select from app.models.link import Link
Every test below takes the `client` fixture, and every test also takes the `db_session` fixture. Both come from tests/conftest.py (L4-004) - do not define them in this file and do not construct a TestClient directly here, because these tests must query the same database the request wrote to.

Test: test_post_link_with_url_and_title_returns_201_and_the_stored_record - `response = client.post("/links", json={"url": "https://example.com/article", "title": "An article"})` - Assert `response.status_code == 201` - `body = response.json()` - Assert `isinstance(body["id"], int)` and `body["id"] > 0` - Assert `body["url"] == "https://example.com/article"` (the submitted url, byte for byte - no trailing slash added, no normalisation) - Assert `body["title"] == "An article"` - Assert `body["created_at"] is not None` and that `datetime.fromisoformat(body["created_at"])` parses without raising - Assert the row was really stored: `db_session.execute(select(func.count()).select_from(Link)).scalar_one() == 1`

Test: test_post_link_with_no_title_stores_null_and_returns_201 - `response = client.post("/links", json={"url": "https://example.com/untitled"})` - Assert `response.status_code == 201` - `body = response.json()` - Assert `"title" in body` - the key must be PRESENT, not omitted - Assert `body["title"] is None` - Assert `body["url"] == "https://example.com/untitled"` - Assert the stored row's title is SQL NULL: `stored = db_session.execute(select(Link)).scalar_one()`, then `assert stored.title is None`

Test: test_post_link_with_no_url_returns_422_and_stores_nothing - `response = client.post("/links", json={})` - Assert `response.status_code == 422` - `response = client.post("/links", json={"title": "A title but no url"})` - Assert `response.status_code == 422` - Assert nothing was stored by EITHER request: `assert db_session.execute(select(func.count()).select_from(Link)).scalar_one() == 0` - The row count is the load-bearing half of this test. A 422 alone does not satisfy the criterion, which says "return 422 AND store nothing".

Test: test_post_link_with_a_non_absolute_http_url_returns_422_and_stores_nothing - For each of these values, post `{"url": value, "title": "Should not be stored"}` and assert the response status is 422: "not-a-url" "/relative/path" "example.com" "ftp://example.com/file.txt" "javascript:alert(1)" "" - After the loop, assert nothing was stored by any of them: `assert db_session.execute(select(func.count()).select_from(Link)).scalar_one() == 0` - As above, the row count is the load-bearing half: the criterion requires 422 AND that nothing is stored.

Test: test_posting_the_same_url_twice_creates_two_rows - Post `{"url": "https://example.com/same"}` twice - Assert both responses have status 201 - Assert the two response bodies have different `id` values - Assert `db_session.execute(select(func.count()).select_from(Link)).scalar_one() == 2` - This test cites no acceptance criterion. It asserts requirement 7, which comes from save-link's notes/considerations block and is deliberately NOT an acceptance criterion. Recorded here as a requirement test rather than attributed to a criterion it does not come from.
